sentences.text: Fa/9/2023 on 7 October, 2025

Author: Rakesh Thapliyal
Bench: Rakesh Thapliyal
 Office Notes, reports,
 orders or proceedings
Sl.
 Date or directions and Court'S Or Judges'S Order
S No  Registrar's order with  Signatures  FA No. 8, 9, 10 AND 11 of 2023  Hon'ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J.
1. Mr. D.S. Patni, learned Sr. Advocate assisted by Mr. Hari Mohan Bhatia and Mr. Siddharath Singh, learned counsel for the appellants.
2. Mr. V. K. Kaparuwan, learned Standing Counsel for the Union of India.
3. Mr. I.P. Kohli, learned Standing Counsel for the State.
4. These four first appeals are arising out of the proceedings initiated under the Land Acquisition Act.

The determination of the compensation on the basis of exampler sale deed was challenged in the Reference Court and the Reference Court rejected the contention of the claimants / appellants and now, these first appeals have been preferred.

5. Appellants of First Appeal No. 11 of 2023 are the actual owner of the land, who purchased the agricultural land by sale deed dated 07.01.2006 and thereafter, the land was declared to be non agricultural land under Section 143 of the U.P.Z.A. & L.R. Act by Assistant Collector on 28.09.2006 and 13.10.2008.

Thereafter, certain part of the land was sold by registered sale deed dated 25.08.2008 and by two another sale deed dated 03.06.2008 to persons who are appellants in First Appeal Nos. 8, 9 and 10 of 2023.

The actual owner of the land also purchased another piece of land by sale deed dated 06.11.2006 which was never part of the acquisition proceedings and the land,
which was purchased by sale deed dated 07.01.2006 was acquired.

6. Learned counsel for the appellants argued that the SLAO took the exampler sale deed of 06.11.2006 of agricultural land, which was not acquired in the acquisition proceedings and as such,
the exampler sale deed in respect of the agricultural land, which was not included in the acquisition proceedings is apparently unjustified and improper.
FA/9/2023 on 7 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34225241/
1 7.

Learned counsel for the appellants further argued that land which was acquired is in fact was non agricultural land and therefore, there is no justification on the part of the SLAO to take sale deed of agricultural land to be exemplar for determination of compensation.

8. On the other side, Mr. V.K. Kaparuwan, learned Standing Counsel for Union of India, submits that Section 4 Notification was issued on 05.01.2009 and thereafter, by another Notification dated 21.12.2009, urgency clause in terms of Section 17 was invoked and before issuance of acquisition notification process was initiated by carrying out survey on the land purposed to be acquired.
He further argued that claimants / appellants raised objection for such acquisition and that aspect has been dealt by the Reference Court in its judgment.

He further argued that appellants were well versed with the proposed acquisition and that is the reason appellants in connivance with Tehsildar,
Haldwani got the agricultural land converted to non agricultural land under Section 143 of the U.P.Z.A. & L.R. Act, which is based on the report of the Tehsildar, Haldwani, who submitted NOC during survey proceedings.
9.
For adjudication of all these first appeals, First Appeal No. 11 of 2023 filed by the owner of the property is being treated as leading one.

10. Learned counsel for the appellants and learned Standing Counsel for the Union of India submit that State Authorities may be directed to produce five sale deeds of non agricultural land, which are in vicinity of the village, of which land is acquired.
11. For this purposes, Mr. I.P. Kohli, learned Standing Counsel for the State prays for and is granted four weeks time to place the five sale deed of non agricultural land on record.

12. In addition to this Mr. Siddharath Singh, learned counsel for the appellants in FA No. 11 of 2023 may also place on record original sale deed dated 07.01.2006.
13.
(Rakesh Thapliyal, J.) 07.10.2025
